verdict.root_cause: The paymentservice request path stayed healthy throughout: charges were received and completed in ~1ms with no error lines, and every Charge span was sub-millisecond with no error status. What broke at onset was telemetry export. Five minutes before the 16:36:15 alert, platform-automation set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT to http://127.0.0.1:4317 on paymentservice, pointing the OTLP trace exporter at loopback where no collector listens. The trace stream shows a step change, not a ramp: full 36-42 span traces to 16:29:48, then one truncated 8-span trace, then 8-9 minutes of silence; checkoutservice's error ratio collapses from a noisy ~0.16 baseline to a flat zero-variance 0 across 129 incident samples, the signature of spans no longer arriving rather than of a system becoming perfect. The failure is an observability blackout caused by a config value that is itself wrong - an exporter endpoint naming an address with no receiver.
verdict.reasoning: Logs [tr_8a0b0bdb0cd0] show info-only paired charge/completion lines running to the end of the window, ruling out crash-loop, credential rejection and charge-path failure. Traces [tr_db859f4b8caf] rule out paymentservice latency and errors and characterise onset as abrupt truncation of span export. checkoutservice metrics [tr_41fae3883547] invert the expected direction - errors existed before the window and went to exact zero with zero variance during it - better explained by spans ceasing to be recorded. The change log [tr_3a9d2f12f403] supplies the mechanism and contains no deploy, image or payment-critical config edit; checkoutservice has no changes at all [tr_c8f537ccb806]. Not bad_deploy because no artifact changed; not dependency_latency because nothing in the request path waited. Confidence is medium: four prior identical toggles were reverted without an attributed incident [tr_3a9d2f12f403], and paymentservice's own error-ratio series is empty in both windows [tr_5058419370b8].
open_questions: Whether any user-facing failure occurred at all - every dispatch found the request path healthy, and no frontend success-rate evidence was gathered.
Whether the export loss is confined to paymentservice or is collector-wide; no collector health was queried, and a collector outage would produce the same shape.
Roughly 16:06-16:36 of the paymentservice log stream is unobserved due to truncation [tr_8a0b0bdb0cd0], and no latency percentiles or saturation were returned for either service.

alternatives.root_cause: A collector- or pipeline-side telemetry outage stopped ingestion for multiple services, and the endpoint toggle is coincidental automation noise.
alternatives.why_not: Explains the breadth as well, but no collector was dispatched, and it does not account for a change 5 minutes before onset that specifically repoints the exporter at loopback [tr_3a9d2f12f403].

alternatives.root_cause: A real slowdown on the shippingservice-to-quoteservice hop degraded checkout and paymentservice merely noticed it.
alternatives.why_not: That hop dominated self-time but root latencies stayed flat at 22-36ms with no ramp through onset [tr_db859f4b8caf]; neither service was dispatched, so this is unexamined rather than supported.

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring paymentservice's prior environment (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT back to unset, i.e. the pre-16:30:31 configuration) should make the trace stream resume. Observable as: (a) Tempo returns paymentservice-participating checkout traces with timestamps after the revert, and those traces are structurally complete again (~36-42 spans, containing Charge, ShipOrder, EmptyCart and email spans) rather than the 8-span truncation last seen at 16:29:48; (b) the checkoutservice span error-ratio series regains non-zero variance around its ~0.16 pre-incident baseline instead of the flat sd=0 zero across the incident window. The payment request path itself should show no change — charge-received/transaction-complete pairs at ~1ms continue uninterrupted apart from the container recreate.
proposal.if_wrong: If, 10 minutes after the revert, Tempo still returns no paymentservice or checkout traces while frontend traffic is demonstrably still flowing (payment logs still show charge/complete pairs), then the blackout is not the paymentservice exporter endpoint — most likely a collector-wide outage, which no evidence here excludes because collector health was never queried. Equally falsifying: traces resume but checkoutservice error ratio stays pinned at exactly 0 with zero variance, which would mean the flat-zero series had a different cause than missing spans. Note also a real gap in observability: the paymentservice error-ratio series was empty in BOTH baseline and incident windows [tr_5058419370b8], so paymentservice's own Prometheus error ratio cannot be used to confirm or falsify anything here — only traces can.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this recreates a container that is currently serving charges successfully — a service confirmed healthy at the request layer is taken down for the recreate on the strength of a telemetry-only symptom. In-flight charge requests during the recreate will fail; the payment path has no observed problem, so this trades a working service against a metrics gap. Secondary risk: ~30 minutes of paymentservice logs (16:06-16:36) are unobserved [tr_8a0b0bdb0cd0], so a real error burst in that interval cannot be excluded, and recreating the container discards in-process state that might carry it. Third: the change history shows this variable flapping on a 5-6 hour automated cadence, so platform-automation will very likely re-apply the loopback endpoint within hours; this revert is symptomatic and does not stop the loop. The durable fix — disabling or correcting the automation that sets this value — is outside what this system may do.
proposal.blast_radius: paymentservice's container is recreated. checkoutservice, its direct caller in the dependency graph, sees connection resets for the duration of the recreate; frontend sees those as failed PlaceOrder attempts one hop further up. The reverted value is a telemetry exporter address, not a business dependency, so no downstream service gains or loses request traffic — but the OTLP collector at the correct endpoint will begin receiving paymentservice spans again, which is the intended effect and will change what every trace-derived metric for paymentservice and checkoutservice reports.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on paymentservice with checkout and frontend downstream cannot be dismissed, and no open incident could absorb it. Nothing in the single seed alert points to a specific fault class yet.
